newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said on Tuesday.
"Government securities were narrowly mixed again today amid continued uncertainty over the near-term direction of the market," a local dealer said.
"Treasury bill yields were slightly lower but bond prices were slightly higher. The interbank rate rose slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Volume was moderate," he said.
In treasury bills, three-months ended at 0.90/0.85 percent compared with Monday's yield of 0.97/0.92 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.48/1.43 percent against 1.57/1.52 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 closed at S$99.08/98.13 from Monday's close of S$99.02/99.07, September 2001 at S$97.35/40 versus S$97.25/97.30 and June 2003 at $S95.35/95.40 against S$95.25/95.30.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 2-3/8 2-1/4 percent from Monday's 3-1/4 3-1/8 percent.
